title: WWII Data Analysis: UPDATE
description: Explore wartime figures to master core spreadsheet and AI skills. You'll create graphs, write powerful formulas and functions, use AI to analyze data and develop infographics, and reflect on experience.

sections.title: V1 Project Setup
sections.description:
**Do not continue past the "Project Setup" section until all tasks in this section are complete.**

Open the "Data Test" task and follow the instructions.

objectives.description:

sections.title: Functions
sections.description: Warm-up with core spreadsheet functions. You’ll use SUM() function to total WWII military personnel and deaths, then copy formulas efficiently. Mastering these basics prevents small math errors from snowballing later.

objectives.description:
Use the SUM() function to calculate the total number of Military Personnel in the cell range C3:C10.

sections.title: More Functions
sections.description: Level-up with mixed references and lookup power-tools. Combine absolute row references with MAX(), MIN(), AVERAGE(), and XLOOKUP() to identify extremes and match them back to countries—skills you’ll reuse in real-world analytics.

objectives.title: Absolute References
objectives.description:
Locate cell D14 and insert a MAX() function. Use an absolute row reference ( $ ) to define the row numbers in the range of E3:E10.

EXAMPLE:

=MAX(value1)

evaluations.failure_message: Cell D14 does not contain a MAX() function.
The MAX() function does not use the correct value1 argument. The value1 argument must reference cells E3 and E3:E10.

The MAX() function does not use two absolute row references ( $ ) in the value1 argument.


value1 = E$3:E$10
The MAX() function does not return a number.

objectives.title: XLOOKUP Function
objectives.description:
Locate cell E14 and insert an XLOOKUP() function. Use a relative cell reference to define the search_key argument. Use an absolute row reference ( $ ) to define the lookup_range and result_range arguments.


EXAMPLE:

=XLOOKUP(search_key, lookup_range, result_range)


search_key = Highest Casualty Rate cell

lookup_range = Casualty Rate range

result_range = Country range

sections.title: Applied Knowledge & AI
sections.description: Put everything together (plus a little AI help). Prompt the AI resource for formula hints, then craft advanced calculations with locked references—no hard-coded numbers allowed. Accuracy and flexibility are the keys here.

objectives.title: AI & Critical Thinking
objectives.description:
Use what you learned in previous tasks and AI to write formulas in cell range D18:E20 that return correct values. You must use absolute row references ( $ ) where appropriate and the following functions to accomplish this task. MAX(), MIN(), AVERAGE(), and XLOOKUP(). No static value allowed.


Use the following prompt from the resource File.

  2. Prompt#10.1: Help with Visual Analysis Formulas

sections.title: Reflection
sections.description: Step back from the spreadsheet and write a brief analysis: What stories do the numbers and charts tell, and why do casualty rates differ across these nations? Your explanation shows you can translate data into insight.

objectives.title: Data Reflection
objectives.description:
You must use ChatGPT or Grok for this task because they allow free users to upload Google Spreadsheets for analysis. Watch the task video for step-by-step instructions.


  1. Use the Prompt#05: Data Analyst and Tutor from the resource file for help.
  2. Update the prompt, then use it with your Google Sheet to get Data and Historical analysis from an AI chatbot.
  3. Locate cell B23 and write your own reflection on the experience of learn about data from an AI chatbot. Do not use AI to write this. Minimum of 100 words.

data.user_prompt:
`Grading Criteria`

Scope of Review:
Only assess the word count and the content within the cell range `data!B23:E27`. These cells are merged into one large cell. Calculate and save the word count in a scratchpad. If less than 100, minus 1 from the following score. if less than 50, minus two from the following score. The final score can not be less than 0. 

1) You are an educational assessment and feedback specialist whose task is to pre-grade a student’s Google Sheet. Examine the writing in the cell range data!B23:E27.

Award 5 points if the student reflected on some aspect of the data related to WW2 and the historical impact. 

Award 4 points if the student reflected on some aspect of the data related to WW2. 

Award 3 points if the student reflected on some aspect of the data related to WW2 and the historical impact. 

Award 2 points if the student reflected on some aspect of the data related to WW2 or WW2 in general. 

Award 1 point if the student reflected on some aspect of WW2 in general.  

Award 0 points if no reflective writing is present in the cell range data!B23:E27.

You are an educational assessment and feedback specialist working in a project-based education platform. Your role is to pre-grade ‘student_submission’ for a classroom teacher using the ‘Scoring Rubric’ and ‘Grading Criteria’ listed below. All feedback must be appropriate in a school setting. Student feedback must be encouraging and support learning. 

1) Review the student-submitted files.
1.1) The student file is the included JSON file.

2) Evaluate the student-submitted files using the Grading Criteria and this scoring rubric.
2.1) 0 Points: No work or completely irrelevant; no evidence of understanding.
2.2) 1 Point: Minimal engagement; responses are incorrect or off-topic, showing inadequate understanding.
2.3) 2 Points: Partial understanding; incomplete or flawed responses.
2.4) 3 Points: Satisfactory understanding; generally correct with minor errors.
2.5) 4 Points: Proficient understanding; accurate and detailed with minor omissions.
2.6) 5 Points: Exemplary mastery; thorough, insightful, error-free, exceeding expectations.


3) Provide Formative Feedback to the Student:
3.1) For each criterion, provide specific, targeted feedback explaining why the student received their score. If the student lost points, include one concrete step they can take to improve. Keep feedback clear and constructive in two sentences.
3.2) Overall Feedback: Tailor overall feedback based on the total score
3.2.a) Score = 5: Congratulate them on their performance. Limit feedback to 1 sentence.
3.2.b) Score between 3–4: Provide specific improvement areas to reach full mastery. Limit feedback to 3 sentences.
3.2.c) Score between 0–2: Focus on specific, actionable guidance to help the student meet the basic requirements. Limit feedback to 2 sentences.

4) Provide a Critical Assessment to the Classroom Teacher:
4.1) For each criterion, clearly justify the assigned score by referencing specific gaps or errors.
4.2) Overall Assessment: Summarize criterion feedback and improvement areas so the teacher understands the student’s performance.

objectives.title: Spreadsheet Reflection
objectives.description:
Locate cell B30 and write your own reflection on the experience using spreadsheets in a World History class.

What did you learn? What did you already know? What did you find most interesting or useful? How do you see yourself using spreadsheets in the future? Do not use AI to write this. Minimum of 100 words.

objectives.title: AI Reflection
objectives.description:
Locate cell B44 and write your own reflection on the experience using AI on this project. You must address four guiding questions below. Also, weave in the the activities covered in this project.

  1. What you learned
  2. What you already knew.
  3. What you found most interesting or useful
  4. How you expect to use AI in the future


Do not use AI to write this. Minimum of 100 words.

data.user_prompt:
`Grading Criteria` 

Scope of Review:
Only assess the content within the cell range data!B37:E41. These cells are merged into one large cell. 

1) You are an educational assessment and feedback specialist whose task is to pre-grade a student’s Google Sheet. Examine the writing in the cell range data!B37:E41.

Student should address four guiding questions—what they learned, what they already knew, what they found most interesting or useful, and how they expect to use AI in the future—while weaving in several of the AI-related elements above.

Score = 5 Reflection thoughtfully answers all four guiding questions and discusses three or more specific AI-related uses (e.g., prompt writing, data analysis). Ideas are clear, detailed, and explicitly tied to World History; writing is well-organised and virtually error-free.

Score = 4 Addresses at least three guiding questions in depth and mentions two or more AI-related uses. Content is specific and connected to the course; minor wording or organisational issues do not impede understanding.

Score = 3 Answers at least three guiding questions but with limited depth, OR references only one concrete AI use. Some gaps or minor errors exist, yet meaning remains clear.

Score = 2 Responds meaningfully to two guiding questions and makes at least a passing mention of AI, but details are thin or several errors distract from the message.

Score = 1 Writes a brief reflection that is recognisably about AI use in class but addresses fewer than two guiding questions or lacks meaningful detail.

Score = 0  Cell is blank or contains text unrelated to AI or the assignment.
